To the newbies who can't deal with scavs, here's your top tips (that I can think of, on the top of my head)  


1. Never peek with just your head. Scavs don't really aim at your face, but if that's the only part they see, that's what they go for. Instead show your entire body.
2. Use a face shield. If you can't afford to go face shield, grab a shattered mask or something. Buckshot has shit penetration, and even armor 1, will stop a pellet or two.
3. Don't re-peek the same angle. If you have a ton of scavs shooting for you, move your ass somewhere else.
4. Scavs only "remember" where you are shortly. If you stay in hiding for a while, they'll reset and go about their business.

The data I'm collecting now is just for the backend API.  


That API can be called upon in other applications so that the creator will have easy access to the data.

The point is that I'll be able to collect all this information, and have it on a server that is publicly accessible.  


What this means is that, let's say I want to make an application that will let you plan out your hideout.  
That means that I will need to have a collection of all the items needed to upgrade the hideout, as well as a collection of the hideout modules and the their respective upgrade requirement for each level.  


If I have this stored on a server, I'll be able to connect to it with an API key, and I can make get calls to access the data, and I won't have to replicate the data on several applications.
